hints: Look closely at the reaction conditions, cold, dilute and acidified, as they tell you whether oxidation will be mild or vigorous.
Count the reactive groups in geraniol, it has two C=C double bonds plus one primary alcohol group.
Recall what cold dilute manganate(VII) does to a C=C bond versus what it does to an alcohol, then apply that to both double bonds.
walkthrough:
**Spot the functional groups in geraniol**

Geraniol contains two separate alkene $\text{C=C}$ groups and one primary alcohol $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Both types could be oxidised, but the conditions decide which reaction happens.

Structure idea:
$$\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=CH-  +  -C(CH}_3\text{)=CH-CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Recall what cold, dilute manganate(VII) does**

Cold, dilute, acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ is a mild oxidising agent. It hydroxylates alkenes by adding one $\text{-OH}$ to each carbon of the double bond to form a diol.

General change:
$$\text{C=C + [O] + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH(OH)-CH(OH)}$$

**Check the alcohol group under these mild conditions**

Oxidation of a primary alcohol to an aldehyde and then to a carboxylic acid needs hot, concentrated oxidising agent with heating or reflux. Cold, dilute conditions leave the $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group unchanged.

**Apply to both double bonds**

Each of the two $\text{C=C}$ bonds in geraniol gains two $\text{-OH}$ groups. The carbon skeleton does not break, and the original primary alcohol stays as $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. This gives a penta-ol with four new $\text{-OH}$ groups plus the original one.

options.A: Correct. Both C=C bonds have undergone mild hydroxylation to $\text{C(OH)-C(OH)}$, giving two diol units, while the primary $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is unchanged. The skeleton is intact, which matches cold, dilute manganate(VII) chemistry.
options.B: Incorrect. This shows hydroxy-ketones and a carboxylic acid, implying further oxidation of the diols and the primary alcohol. That level of oxidation requires hot, concentrated conditions, not cold and dilute.
options.C: Incorrect. This shows three small cleavage fragments (propanone and carboxylic acids). This is the trap for hot, concentrated acidified manganate(VII) which cleaves C=C bonds completely. Cold, dilute reagent does not break the carbon chain.
options.D: Incorrect. This shows only the primary alcohol oxidised to $-\text{COOH}$ while both C=C bonds are untouched. In reality alkenes are very readily attacked by cold dilute $\text{MnO}_4^-$, and the alcohol would not be oxidised under these mild conditions.
